entities.name: Lucius Sestius Albanianus Quirinalis
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Sestius Albanianus Quirinalis, a prominent aristocrat of the late Roman Republic, played a pivotal role in the transition from the Republic to the Empire.

Appointed suffect consul in 23 BC, he filled the role of his predecessor, Gaius Cornelius Lentulus Gaus, and served alongside Augustus as a symbol of the Empire's unity.

Despite his Republican tendencies, Albanianus Quirinalis's appointment underscores the complex power dynamics of the late Republic and the increasing influence of the imperial administration.

This appointment also highlights the fluidity of Roman politics, as Albanianus Quirinalis, a member of the noble class, accepted the role of consul, a position traditionally held by the aristocracy.
